name: PlayCanvas Engine
role: Open-source web 3D engine usable standalone; strong glTF and Gaussian splat support
summary: MIT-licensed WebGL2 and WebGPU engine with an entity-component model, PBR, glTF, physics integration and Gaussian splat rendering. Used as a standalone npm library from code, without the PlayCanvas Editor. Distinguishing strength: small runtime footprint, game-style structure and splat support.
use_when: Over Three.js for Gaussian splat scenes with an engine-native renderer
Over Babylon.js when a smaller runtime and entity-component structure fit
Game-like scenes with scripts and components rather than one-off shots
avoid_when: Ecosystem tooling like postprocessing, drei or R3F: Three.js
Render-once-per-seek control: Three.js is simpler to drive

evidence.result: 90 distinct 1280x720 alpha frames at 30 fps; all shuffled hashes equal sequential in two runs; hashes identical across runs; frame 45 alpha min 0 max 1. Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 156.0.8078.4, Node 22.19.0; screenshot route, WebGL2 context. Contact sheet inspected at native size.
evidence.scope: PlayCanvas box, sphere and cylinder set from t per seek, lit, transparent camera; alpha PNG on WebGL2, macOS arm64. No app.start(), WebGPU, splats or scripts.

notes: 2026-10-26: determinism of the engine update loop under external seeking was not verified; splat support is from memory.

assessment.rationale: Frequent npm releases through Oct 2026; MIT; engine is usable without the cloud editor. Overlaps Three.js and Babylon.js with a game-engine slant.
